text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.6% today as oil prices spiked to six-month highs on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $116 per barrel following reports that the U.S. is preparing strikes against Iran and withdrawing diplomats from Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on oil infrastructure. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost profitability on the barrels they produce and sell.

The stock's broader two-week gain of 12.5% reflects a sustained rally in energy prices driven by geopolitical risk in the region — the same tensions that pushed Brent crude from around $110 in early October to $116 today. This shift is reshaping global energy markets and benefits U.S. energy producers and exporters, which is why the energy sector has been outperforming.
